name: Ferrite Dust
tips: Mine from any rocky outcrop on any planet — it is everywhere. Never sell it; almost every crafting recipe calls for it directly or indirectly. Always carry a full stack.

name: Pure Ferrite
tips: Refine Ferrite Dust 1:1 in any portable refiner — free upgrade. Keep a stack ready; building and tech upgrades will consume it constantly.

name: Magnetised Ferrite
tips: Craft by refining Pure Ferrite together with metals (e.g. Gold or Silver). Only needed for specific advanced builds — don't stockpile until a recipe actually calls for it.

name: Carbon
tips: Harvest from any plant or tree. It fuels your mining laser — the tool you use to gather everything else — so running out is a real problem. Always keep at least half a stack.

name: Condensed Carbon
tips: Refine Carbon 2:1 to produce Condensed Carbon, which burns longer per unit. Also drops from red crystals on planetary surfaces. Worth making early once you have a portable refiner.

name: Di-hydrogen
tips: Blue crystals scattered on nearly every planet surface. Without it your ship can't take off — stock up before leaving on a long expedition. Refine 5 into Di-hydrogen Jelly for a more storage-efficient fuel form.

name: Oxygen
uses: Refining catalyst (doubles output of many recipes)
tips: Collect from red plants or buy cheaply at stations. Beyond keeping you alive, Oxygen acts as a free catalyst in the refiner — combine it with Chlorine to duplicate it endlessly, a classic early money loop.

name: Sodium
tips: Harvest from yellow plants on any planet. Use it to recharge your hazard protection module during storms or toxic/heat exposure. Always carry a stack when exploring hostile worlds.

name: Sodium Nitrate
tips: Refine Sodium at a 2:1 ratio to get Sodium Nitrate, which restores twice as much hazard protection. Well worth the refiner time before heading to extreme-weather planets.

name: Cobalt
tips: Abundant in caves on most planets; guaranteed on irradiated worlds. Decent sell value in bulk. Also works as a simple trade-route item: buy cheap at one station and sell at a station with a market bonus.

name: Ionised Cobalt
uses: Crafting Ion Batteries & Advanced Ion Batteries
tips: Refine Cobalt 1:1 for a free value bump. Crafting Ion Batteries from it yields even more units per stack. A solid early money-maker if you farm caves aggressively.

name: Pyrite
tips: Found on desert and scorched planet types. Not particularly lucrative to sell; keep a small buffer for planet-specific crafting recipes you will encounter during story progression.

name: Dioxite
uses: Crafting Cryogenic Chamber and related components
tips: Only found on frozen/icy planets. If a recipe calls for it and you are far from a frozen world, check space station traders. Stock up whenever you visit a frozen planet.

name: Paraffinium
tips: Harvested from yellow-flowering plants on lush and warm continental planets. Important for base building. If your home planet lacks it, either trade for it or keep a supply from a nearby lush world.

name: Phosphorus
tips: Found on scorched and fiery planet types. Needed for specific tech and weapons — keep a small stock. (unsicher: exact planet type distribution can vary between game updates)

name: Ammonia
tips: Exclusive to toxic planets. It is a key ingredient in the high-value Stasis Device crafting chain later in the game. Stock up during any toxic planet visit — they appear infrequently in some systems.

name: Cactus Flesh
tips: Harvested from cactus plants on desert planets. Sells reasonably well and any surplus refines to Carbon for fuel. Not a critical crafting material early on — sell what you don't need.

name: Star Bulb
tips: From Star Bramble plants on lush planets — they grow in clusters, so a quick run yields a large stack. Refines into Paraffinium if you need it, but selling is often more efficient early on.

name: Mordite
tips: Drops from almost any creature you kill. Accumulates naturally during exploration. Low individual value — sell in batches or refine to Carbon. (unsicher: exact sell value per unit varies by market)

name: Copper
uses: Base of the Chromatic Metal multiplication chain
tips: Mine from Copper deposits found near Electromagnetic Hotspots (scan for hotspots with your Analysis Visor). The primary early source of Chromatic Metal — the material that goes into nearly every piece of tech.

name: Chromatic Metal
uses: Required by almost all technology crafting recipes
tips: Produced by refining any stellar metal (Copper, Cadmium, Emeril, Indium). Do not sell it — nearly every technology component calls for it. Keep a running stock of at least 200-300 units.

name: Gold
uses: Crafting electrical components and Warp Drive parts
Refining catalyst for Chromatic Metal (boosts ratio)
tips: Found in asteroids and underground cave deposits. Needed for Warp Drive components and other critical tech — keep a buffer of at least 50 units before selling surplus. Sells well in emergencies.

name: Silver
uses: Refining catalyst (boosts Chromatic Metal output from stellar metals)
tips: Mined from underground cave deposits. Good sell value and less critical for crafting than Gold. Sell the bulk; keep only a small amount (~50) for refining combos with stellar metals.

name: Platinum
uses: Refining chain involving Nanites (unsicher: verify current recipe)
tips: One of the best raw resources for earning units early. Worth ~505 units each, so even a modest haul converts to significant funds. Sell freely — there is rarely a crafting bottleneck on Platinum.

name: Activated Indium
tips: Found only on planets orbiting blue-coloured stars — you need a Cadmium Drive → Emeril Drive → Indium Drive upgrade chain to reach blue systems. At ~949 units per item it is the highest-value raw resource in the game. A large automated mine here is the classic mid-game unit farm.
